input.question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?
input.ground_truth: America didn't get bombed and saw *immense* federal spending that ended the great depression. Also, as it turns out, being the only industrial power that didn't get bombed to hell makes your economy pretty strong as there isn't a whole lot of competition.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a big game together. You all have some toys and candies to start with. But then, a big storm (that’s like World War 2) comes and messes up everyone’s toys and candies.

Now, after the storm, one of your friends (let’s call him America) still has a lot of his toys and candies left because he wasn’t as hurt by the storm. He even helped fix some things for his friends while the storm was happening. So after the storm, America has lots of toys and candies to play with and even to share a little.

But the other friends (like Europe and Asia) lost most of their toys and candies during the storm. Their houses were broken, and they didn’t have enough to play with anymore.

Because America still had lots of toys and candies, he could build new things and help his friends a little. But his friends didn’t have enough to start building again right away, so it took them a long time to get their toys and candies back.

That’s kind of how it was after World War 2: America’s economy was still strong, but many other countries were poor and needed help to get better.
